text: 4IN and 4OF are ways to loop through objects and arrays. 4IN loops through property names of an object. Remember that objects are made up of property or key value pairs. So here we have an object called posts and in this object we have the properties of id, title and body. Next to those are the values of each. This is the basic syntax of a 4IN loop. We start with the keyword for, then within parentheses we create a variable. Then we have the keyword in. Then we include the object that we are iterating through. After that will be our execution code within curly braces. So using our posts object we can set it up like this. The variable that we are creating will call post and then in posts which is the object. Now when we console log the post variable we are getting all of the properties or keys. In order to get the values we will need to reference the original object posts and use square brackets to define the property. Now in our console log we are getting all of the values. 4IN will work with an array. Instead of a named property it will use the index of each value. So here we are getting 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 in our console. We can see that those are the indices of each value. In order to get the values we would have to reference the original array and use square brackets to define the index of the value. A better solution would be to use for of. For of loops iterate through items in a collection such as an array. Here is the basic syntax of a for of loop. It's very similar to the 4IN except this time we are using the of keyword and passing it an iterable instead of an object. So if we use a for of loop with this array then we will not have to reference the original array using indices. It will just give us the value directly. Note that for of will not work with objects because they are not iterable. And just remember that 4IN is for objects and 4OF is for arrays. This has been a 90ish second JavaScript January.
